Month one
Vidya: Sir, should I use the random forest or the regression? What would you choose?
Raghav: What do you think, and why?
Vidya: Regression, I guess. Whatever you'd pick, honestly
Raghav: I'd rather hear your reasoning first.

Month four
Vidya: I tested both. Regression is simpler and the gap is tiny, so I'm going with it. One thing I disagree with from last month's suggestion: the outlier rule. The data shows it drops real cases.
Raghav: Good catch. I'd change my rule. Thanks 🙂
Vidya: I was nervous to say it 😊
Raghav: You don't need my sign-off on this one. Show me if you want a second pair of eyes.

qa.a: Vidya disagreed with the outlier rule from last month's suggestion.

qa.q: What did Vidya want when saying "Whatever you'd pick, honestly"?
qa.a: Vidya wanted Raghav to decide, which shows both admiration and a habit of depending on the mentor.

qa.q: How did Raghav help Vidya grow?
qa.a: Raghav asked for Vidya's reasoning first, welcomed the disagreement and said the sign-off was not needed.

qa.q: How might Raghav have felt when Vidya corrected the rule?
qa.a: Raghav was probably pleased and even proud, since Raghav thanked Vidya and offered a second pair of eyes only if wanted.

grounding: A young adult learns from a mentor and gradually forms an own judgement, moving toward peer respect.

passage:
In the carpentry shed behind Nandgaon market, Tejas had spent two years at Anirban's side. He copied the way Anirban held a chisel, the way he tested wood with a knuckle. If a customer asked him anything, he said, "Ask Anirban-da."

Then Anirban went to his daughter's wedding for a week, and the headmaster came with a broken school bench. Tejas looked at the cracked leg and heard Anirban's voice in his head: replace it. But the wood was sound; only the joint had failed. He decided to re-glue and pin it instead, and it held.

When Anirban came back, Tejas showed him the bench, braced for a scolding. Anirban pushed on it with his full weight. "I would have replaced the leg," he said. "Your way saves the school money. Good call."

The next month, when they disagreed about a door frame, Anirban said, "Convince me." Tejas did.

qa.q: Why did Anirban go away for a week?
qa.a: Anirban went to his daughter's wedding.

qa.q: What was Tejas feeling when he showed Anirban the repaired bench?
qa.a: Tejas felt nervous and braced for a scolding, unsure whether trusting his own judgement had been right.

qa.q: Which choice showed Tejas growing beyond dependence, and why did it work?
qa.a: Tejas trusted his own reading of the wood and re-glued the joint instead of copying Anirban, and the repair held.

qa.q: How does Anirban seem to see Tejas by the end?
qa.a: Anirban seems to respect Tejas as a peer, asking Tejas to convince him instead of simply giving orders.

grounding: Shows a young apprentice who admired and depended on a mentor forming his own judgement, ending in mutual respect.

passage:
For a year at the Accra design studio, Kofi had run every decision past Chidi. Which font, which colour, whether a client email sounded polite enough. Chidi always answered, patiently, and Kofi always did exactly that.

In March a school asked for a new logo. Chidi sketched a bold shield. Kofi looked at it for a long time and felt his stomach knot. It looked like a bank, not a school for small children.

He could have just drawn the shield. Instead he made a second version: rounded letters, a small open book. At the meeting he said, "I think yours is strong, but I'm worried it feels too serious for the parents. Can I show another option?"

Chidi studied both. "You're right," she said. "Show the client yours first."

The client chose Kofi's. That evening Chidi asked his opinion on her own project, and she actually used it.

qa.q: What did Kofi's second logo include?
qa.a: Kofi's logo had rounded letters and a small open book.

qa.q: What was Kofi feeling when he first looked at Chidi's shield?
qa.a: Kofi felt uneasy and conflicted, with a knotted stomach, because he disagreed with his mentor for the first time.

qa.q: What did Kofi do that a young worker could learn from?
qa.a: He respectfully named his concern and offered a clear alternative instead of either copying his mentor or staying silent.

qa.q: How does Chidi see Kofi after the meeting?
qa.a: Chidi seems to see Kofi as a colleague whose judgement is worth using, since she asks his opinion on her own project.

grounding: Shows a young designer moving from dependence on an admired mentor to own judgement, ending in peer respect.
